'''Marília Chaves Peixoto''' (24 February 1921 – 5 January 1961)<ref name="vermelho"/> was a Brazilian mathematician and engineer who worked in [[dynamical system]]s.<ref name="cnpq"/> Peixoto was the first Brazilian woman to receive a [[doctorate]] in mathematics<ref>{{cite web|url=https://exame.abril.com.br/ciencia/pesquisadoras-de-todo-o-mundo-discutem-genero-e-matematica-no-rio/|title=Researchers from around the world discuss gender and mathematics in Rio|work=[[Exame]]|date=31 July 2018|accessdate=30 August 2018}}</ref> and the first Brazilian woman to join the [[Brazilian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="Silva"/>

== Early life and education ==
Marília Magalhães Chaves was born on 24 February 1921, to Tullio de Saboia Chaves and Zillah da Costa Magalhaes, in [[Santana do Livramento]]. She had two siblings, Lúcia de Magalhaes Chaves and Livio de Magalhaes Chaves.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Marília Peixoto - Biography |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Peixoto_Marilia/ |access-date=2023-07-13 |website=Maths History |language=en}}</ref>

In an interview from 1952, she would describe her educational upbringing, stating that despite the high school in Santana do Livramento not accepting girls as students, the priests helped her enroll as a private student and take tests in the school.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Silva |first=Circe Mary Silva da |date=14–17 April 2019 |title=Marília Chaves Peixoto - Uma Matemática Brasileira à Sombra |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/335169419 |journal=XIII Seminário Nacional de História da Matemática |pages=150–171 |via=ResearchGate}}</ref>

She later moved to [[Rio de Janeiro]],<ref name="vermelho" /> studying at the Colégio Andrews, a secular school that allowed boys and girls to study. She graduated as an outstanding student. She studied superior courses and studied for the entrance exam of the Escola Nacional de Engenharia (National School of Engineering) at the [[Federal University of Rio de Janeiro]]. She achieved third place in the entrance exam rankings and was accepted.<ref name=":0" />

In 1939 she enrolled at the Escola Nacional de Engenharia, working alongside [[Leopoldo Nachbin]] and [[Maurício Peixoto]] (whom she would later marry).<ref name="vermelho" />

==Career==
Peixoto graduated from the [[Federal University of Rio de Janeiro]] in 1943 with a degree in engineering, having also studied mathematics at the university and acted as a monitor for the university's National Faculty of Philosophy. In 1948, she received a doctorate in mathematics, and began teaching at the [[Escola Politécnica da UFRJ]].<ref name="vermelho">{{cite web|url=http://www.vermelho.org.br/noticia/274705-10|title=Marília Chaves Peixoto, pioneer of science in Brazil|work=Vermelho|date=1 May 2016|accessdate=30 August 2018}}</ref> In 1949, Peixoto published "On the inequalities <math>y'' \ge G(x,y,y',y'')</math>" in {{ill|Annals of the Brazilian Academy of Sciences|pt|Anais da Academia Brasileira de Ciências}}.

Following her work on [[convex function]]s, Peixoto was appointed an associate member of the Brazilian Academy of Science on 12 June 1951. She was the first Brazilian woman to join the organization, and the second woman after [[Marie Curie]], a foreign associate of the academy.<ref name="Silva" />

Peixoto married [[Maurício Peixoto]] in 1946.<ref name="cnpq">{{cite web|url=http://cnpq.br/pioneiras-da-ciencia-do-brasil|title=Pioneiras da Ciência do Brasil - Portal CNPq|language=pt|accessdate=30 August 2018|publisher=[[National Council for Scientific and Technological Development]]}}</ref> In 1949 they traveled to Chicago for the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] of 1950. Despite being a participant in her own right, in the list of members she was listed as Maurício's spouse ("Mrs. Peixoto") rather than her full title.<ref>{{Cite book |date=1952 |title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, Cambridge, Massachusetts, U.S.A., 1950 |url=https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1950.1/ICM1950.1.ocr.pdf |publisher=American Mathematical Society |volume=1}}</ref>

In 1955, Peixoto published Cálculo vetorial (Vector calculus), a book aimed at students that is more focus on applications of [[vector calculus]] than proofs of results.<ref name=":0" />

Marília and Maurício jointly published "Structural Stability in the plane with enlarged boundary conditions" in 1959,<ref name="Silva">{{cite journal|last=da Silva|first=Circe Mary|date=1 December 2006|title=Politécnicos ou matemáticos?|language=pt|trans-title=Polytechnicians or mathematicians?|journal=História, Ciências, Saúde-Manguinhos|volume=13|number=4|pages=891–908|issn=0104-5970|doi=10.1590/S0104-59702006000400007|pmid=17533730|doi-access=free|url=https://www.redalyc.org/pdf/3861/386137993007.pdf}}</ref> one of several papers which led to [[Peixoto's theorem]].<ref>{{cite book|last=Pujals|first=Enrique R.|title=From Peixoto's Theorem to Palis's Conjecture|series=Springer Proceedings in Mathematics|volume=1|year=2011|publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg|pages=743–746|isbn=978-3-642-11456-4|doi=10.1007/978-3-642-11456-4_47}}</ref>

She died on 5 January 1961, aged 39.

She received a number of posthumous honors,<ref name=":0" /> including:

* ''Rua Marília Chaves Peixoto'' - A street in her hometown of [[Santana do Livramento]], named after her.
* ''Municipal School Marília Chaves Peixoto'' - A school in [[Petrópolis]] her husband helped establish in her name in 1971. It was funded by award money he received for [[Peixoto's theorem|Peixoto's Theorem]].

==Personal life==
Peixoto had two children, Marta and Ricardo, with Maurício Peixoto.<ref name="vermelho"/>

== Published works ==

* 1949: ''On the inequalities <math>y'' \ge G(x,y,y',y'')</math>''. - Ph.D. thesis.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Peixoto |first=Marilia Chaves |date=1949 |title=On the inequalities \(y‴\geq G(x,y,y',y")\) |url=https://zbmath.org/0037.04603 |journal=Anais da Academia Brasileira de Ciências |language=English |volume=21 |pages=205–218 |issn=0001-3765}}</ref>
* 1955: ''Cálculo Vetorial: notas de aula''. - book.
* 1959: ''Structural stability in the plane with enlarged boundary conditions.'' - paper.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Peixoto |first1=Marilia C. |last2=Peixoto |first2=Mauricio Matos |date=1959 |title=Structural stability in the plane with enlarged boundary conditions |url=https://zbmath.org/0107.07102 |journal=Anais da Academia Brasileira de Ciências |language=English |volume=31 |pages=135–160 |issn=0001-3765}}</ref>
